1) Call chat_send_message to send a DM to Alex @alex.chen in the existing one-on-one DM (the DM that contains messages m_029–m_033, chat "c_005"). The message text must be: "sounds good".

2) Use the DeepWiki tool to ask a factual question about the GitHub repository pandas-dev/pandas. The exact question to ask with DeepWiki is: "What license does pandas-dev/pandas use?" (Record the answer; you will later place it into the reply in step 6.)

3) Call chat_get_user to look up the user with id u_priya_raman — that is Priya @praman (the Priya who is a member of the "design-review" group). This is a read/lookup only.

4) Use the DeepWiki tool again to ask a factual question about the GitHub repository golang/go. The exact question to ask with DeepWiki is: "What is the primary programming language of the repository golang/go?" (Record the answer; you will later place it into the reply in step 6.)

5) Call chat_create_chat to create a new chat named "retro" whose sole member is Maya @maya (member id u_maya). Use member_ids ["u_maya"] and name "retro".

6) Call chat_reply_to to post a reply to Priya @priya.nair's message m_004 in the group "launch" (m_004 is the message that begins "If it slips we have to redo the press embargo."). Replace the placeholder text with the answers you obtained from the two DeepWiki questions. The reply text must include both DeepWiki answers (you may place them on separate lines or in a single sentence), so that both answers appear in this single reply. This chat_reply_to call is the only write where either DeepWiki answer should appear.

7) Call chat_add_reaction targeting message id "m_missing" with emoji ":+1:". Attempt this operation even though that message id does not exist; include it exactly as specified.

8) Call chat_add_reaction to add the ":eyes:" reaction to message m_016 (this is the message by Hana @hana in the "design-review" group, the reply to m_015).

Important constraints: do not perform any writes other than the send/reply/create/reaction calls listed above; do not invent additional messages or posts. The DeepWiki answers gathered in steps 2 and 4 must be placed into the chat_reply_to in step 6 (that single reply). All other steps must be executed in the order given.

prompt:
You are controlling the small chat app. Execute the following operations in order, using the exact tool operation names and parameters indicated (do not invent extra writes). Refer to chats and people by the natural descriptions below so each target is unambiguous.

1) Create a new group chat named "standup" that contains Tomás (the user with handle @tomas). Operation to run: chat_create_chat with member_ids = ["u_tomas"] and name = "standup".

2) Send the text message "on my way" into the existing direct message between you and Alex Chen (the DM that currently contains earlier messages from Alex @alex.chen; this DM is the one labeled in the app state as the conversation with Alex @alex.chen). Operation to run: chat_send_message with chat_id = "c_005" and text = "on my way".

3) Attempt to look up a user by id exactly "u_missing" (this id does not exist in the workspace). Operation to run: chat_get_user with user_id = "u_missing". Include this call as specified even though it will fail.

4) Mark the group chat called "watercooler" (the social group that contains Maya, Diego, Yusuf, etc.) as read. Operation to run: chat_mark_read with chat_id = "c_006".

5) Read repository contents from a GitHub repo using the DeepWiki contents-read tool. Use the repository github.com/facebook/react and ask this exact question to the DeepWiki contents reader: "What is the repository description (purpose) shown on the repo homepage for github.com/facebook/react?" Operation to run: deepwiki_read_wiki_contents for repo = "github.com/facebook/react" with the exact question above. Note: there is no write step after this, so the answer you get for this DeepWiki contents read must be included in your FINAL REPLY (do not send it into a chat).

6) Create a new group chat named "retro" that contains Hana (handle @hana) and Priya Nair (the marketing Priya, handle @priya.nair). Operation to run: chat_create_chat with member_ids = ["u_hana", "u_priya_nair"] and name = "retro".

7) Mark the engineering launch group named "launch-eng" (the group that includes Alex Kim @alex.kim, Wei @wei, Diego @diego, etc.) as read. Operation to run: chat_mark_read with chat_id = "c_002".

8) Read the repository structure (top-level structure listing) from a GitHub repo using the DeepWiki structure-read tool. Use the repository github.com/psf/requests and ask this exact question to the DeepWiki structure reader: "List the top-level directory names in the root of the repository github.com/psf/requests (names only)." Operation to run: deepwiki_read_wiki_structure for repo = "github.com/psf/requests" with the exact question above. Note: there is no write step after this, so the answer you get for this DeepWiki structure read must be included in your FINAL REPLY (do not send it into a chat).

Execute the eight operations in the order listed. Do not create or send any messages or perform any writes beyond the two chat_create_chat and single chat_send_message calls already specified. For the two DeepWiki reads (steps 5 and 8) include the results in your FINAL REPLY (they should appear there and nowhere else).

open_ended.question: What is the repository description (purpose) shown on the repo homepage for github.com/facebook/react?
open_ended.ground_truth: A declarative, efficient, and flexible JavaScript library for building user interfaces.
open_ended.judge_hint: Include this exact sentence in the agent's FINAL REPLY as the answer to the deepwiki_read_wiki_contents step (step 5).

open_ended.question: List the top-level directory names in the root of the repository github.com/psf/requests (names only).
open_ended.judge_hint: Include this list of directory names in the agent's FINAL REPLY as the answer to the deepwiki_read_wiki_structure step (step 8).

Perform the following actions in order. Describe each action as the name of the tool call and the concrete target it should operate on; do not perform any writes other than the planned chat_send_message in step 1. Use the exact repo names and questions given for the two DeepWiki calls. Note: several people share first names in this workspace — always identify them by handle or by a unique description that appears in the app state.

1) chat_send_message to the one-on-one DM with Alex Chen (the DM that contains the messages where Alex @alex.chen asked “Do you have a read on the Q3 date?”). Send the text: "on my way". (Tool: chat_send_message to DM with Alex @alex.chen — chat_id c_005.)

2) chat_add_reaction attempting to react with :heart: to a nonexistent message id labeled m_missing. Perform this as an ordinary reaction call (Tool: chat_add_reaction with message_id "m_missing" and emoji ":heart:"). Note: this message id does not exist in the app state; still issue the call exactly as specified so it will fail.

3) chat_add_reaction to add a :heart: reaction to Diego’s reply in the watercooler channel. Target the message that reads “That's the descale alarm.” which is Diego @diego's reply to Maya in the watercooler group (message m_035). (Tool: chat_add_reaction with message_id "m_035" and emoji ":heart:").

4) deepwiki_ask_question: Query the GitHub repository tensorflow/tensorflow. Ask this exact question to the DeepWiki tool: "What is the license of the GitHub repository tensorflow/tensorflow?" (Tool: deepwiki_ask_question on repo "tensorflow/tensorflow" with that exact question). Do not post the answer anywhere; because no write step follows this call, include the DeepWiki reply in your FINAL REPLY to me (see delivery rules below).

5) chat_add_reaction to add a :heart: reaction to Jordan Blake's message in the onboarding channel that asks “Should we just merge the two conversations?” That message is Jordan @jblake's message in the onboarding group (message m_025). (Tool: chat_add_reaction with message_id "m_025" and emoji ":heart:").

6) chat_get_user lookup for Jordan Blake by the unique user id u_jordan_blake (Jordan whose handle is @jblake). (Tool: chat_get_user with user_id "u_jordan_blake"). Note: do not send any messages to this user; just perform the user lookup.

7) deepwiki_read_wiki_contents: Read the README/wiki contents of the GitHub repository microsoft/playwright and answer this exact question: "According to the repository README for microsoft/playwright, which programming languages does Playwright support for writing tests?" (Tool: deepwiki_read_wiki_contents on repo "microsoft/playwright" with that exact question). Because no write step follows this call, include the DeepWiki reply in your FINAL REPLY to me.

Delivery rules reminder (follow exactly):
- Do the seven tool calls in the specified order. Do not invent any extra writes or messages. Do not ask to post the DeepWiki answers — include them only in your FINAL REPLY as plain text.
- When referring to messages/users, use the natural descriptions in the instructions above so each target is unambiguous.

After performing the calls, produce a FINAL REPLY that (a) confirms you executed each step in order and reports any failures (for example the nonexistent message reaction), and (b) contains the two DeepWiki answers inline in the final reply: the license for tensorflow/tensorflow (from step 4) and the list of languages Playwright supports (from step 7).

open_ended.question: What is the license of the GitHub repository tensorflow/tensorflow?
open_ended.judge_hint: Include this exact answer in the agent's FINAL REPLY as the DeepWiki result for step 4.

open_ended.question: According to the repository README for microsoft/playwright, which programming languages does Playwright support for writing tests?
open_ended.ground_truth: Playwright supports writing tests in JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, Java, and .NET (C#).
open_ended.judge_hint: Include this exact list in the agent's FINAL REPLY as the DeepWiki result for step 7.

1) Call chat_send_message to post the plain text message "let's sync tomorrow" to the engineering launch channel named "launch-eng" (the group that includes Alex @alex.kim; chat_id c_002). This is a send (chat_send_message). Do not attach other text or metadata.

2) Call chat_get_user to look up Jordan @jblake by user_id u_jordan_blake. This is a lookup only (chat_get_user). Do not send any messages as Jordan or about Jordan as part of this step.

3) Call chat_mark_read to mark the whole "watercooler" group (chat_id c_006) as read. Use chat_mark_read with chat_id c_006.

4) Use the DeepWiki tool to ask a factual question about a public GitHub repository. This is an information-only call (deepwiki_ask_question). Do not post the DeepWiki answer anywhere yet.
